sender.en: A friend, a “school” or “WhatsApp support”; later your own number, messaging your contacts

name.en: WhatsApp takeover: “I sent you a code by mistake”, then your contacts are asked for money

how.en: A scammer poses as a friend, school staff or WhatsApp support and gets you to share the six-digit code WhatsApp sends by SMS, saying it was sent by mistake or is needed to join a group or verify your account. Some use call forwarding or a QR code instead. With the code they take over your WhatsApp and message your contacts asking for urgent money. National CERT warned of a wave of these hijackings in January 2026.

text.en: A friend, school or “support” asks for a code sent to your phone.
You are asked to share the six-digit WhatsApp code or scan a QR code.
You are logged out and the scammer controls your account.
Your contacts get urgent requests for money from your number.
Yaar ghalti se mera code tumhare number par chala gaya hai, 6 digit wala code bhej do please, urgent hai.
Assalam o alaikum, school ki taraf se parents ka naya WhatsApp group bana hai. Join karne ke liye aap ke number par jo code aaya hai wo share kar dein.
Bhai ek emergency hai, abhi 30,000 Easypaisa kar do, shaam tak wapas kar doon ga. Call nahi kar sakta.

en: ghalti se code chala gaya bhej do
whatsapp hacked friends asked for money
school group join karne ke liye code manga
my whatsapp was hacked after sharing code
whatsapp support asked for six digit code
hacked number asking contacts to send money
Anyone asking for a WhatsApp code, even a friend.
A message from a known number asking for money and saying they can’t talk.
Requests to dial a code or scan a QR code for “verification”.
Never share a WhatsApp code; turn on two-step verification.
If hijacked, reinstall WhatsApp and log in with your number to get a new code, and warn your contacts.
Before sending money to a friend, call them on their usual number.

sources.title: National CERT Advisory: Widespread WhatsApp Account Hijacking & Unauthorized Access Incidents
Rising impersonation scams threaten digital economy

story.en: A father in Faisalabad got a call from someone posing as staff at his children’s school, who said a WhatsApp group had been made for parents. After he followed the steps, his account was hacked within minutes, and his friends transferred nearly Rs 150,000 in answer to messages asking for urgent help.
